options: A cap per request, a ledger per tenant, and a router by task shape
A bigger model, more retries, longer prompts
explanation: All three are rules in code wrapped around the call.

stem: A tenant hits its daily budget. Default policy?
options: Degrade — smaller model, shorter answers, queue — and alert; refuse only for abuse
explanation: Refusal turns a cost control into an outage for a paying customer.

options: The shape of the task — classification/extraction to small, judgement/reasoning to large — tuned with eval numbers
explanation: Small models are genuinely good at extraction and classification; measure each route on the golden set.

options: One oversized prompt from costing a fortune or overflowing the window — truncate deliberately or reject
explanation: A ceiling per request is the first line of cost predictability.

options: Try the small model with a schema; escalate to the large one when validation fails or it says not_found
explanation: Cheap first, expensive only when needed — measure the escalation rate.

stem: Before moving a task down a tier you should…
options: Just do it and watch complaints
Measure that route on the golden set
explanation: 'It seemed fine' is not a measurement.

stem: A batch job under a service account burns the shared daily budget at 00:05. Fix?
options: Move everything to the large model
Separate budgets per principal and per kind (users vs jobs); jobs to batch with their own ledger
explanation: Budgets must be per principal and per kind of principal.

options: p95 cost per request above a threshold, or large-model share of traffic rising
explanation: Alerts map to actions: review the router, check the prompt, find the tenant.

stem: Against 'everything to the large model', a budget-and-route policy typically…
options: Cuts the bill substantially and, more importantly, puts a ceiling on every request and tenant
explanation: Predictability is the point; the saving is the bonus.

stem: When is 'everything to the large model' right?
options: Low volume, high stakes, judgement-heavy, no eval set yet — quality first, optimise once you can measure
